sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: The cultivated bulb onion is a bulbous geophyte originating as a crop from Central Asia and now grown widely. Its bulb consists of fleshy leaf bases; the green leaves are cylindrical and hollow, and the flowering stalk can reach 1 m. Numerous white flowers form an umbel, followed by a capsule.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The bulb is eaten as a vegetable. Onion can poison dogs, cats and livestock when enough is ingested. Compared with Allium ampeloprasum, onion has hollow cylindrical leaves and is selected for its bulb, while leek-type forms of A. ampeloprasum have flat leaves.
